title: Service-to-service: client credentials
subtitle: How services call each other and the GL with their own identity
summary: When Race Operations asks Horse Registry about eligibility, or the outbox relay posts an event to the GL, the calling service authenticates as itself with the OAuth2 Client Credentials grant (svc-<module>). Spring Security's authorized-client manager fetches, caches and refreshes the token.

sections.title: Outbox relay to the GL
sections.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant R as Race Operations
  participant DB as integration.accounting_event_outbox
  participant K as Keycloak
  participant G as General Ledger
  R->>DB: INSERT event (same transaction as the entry)
  loop every few seconds
    R->>DB: pick PENDING / SENT rows
    R->>K: client_credentials (svc-racing) - cached
    K-->>R: access token (roles SVC_READ, SVC_GL_POST)
    R->>G: POST /api/v1/accounting-events (Bearer)
    G-->>R: 201 journal id (200 if duplicate)
    R->>DB: status POSTED, journal_id
  end

sections.title: Token provider
Why it matters
items: Each service has its own identity and secret (svc-<module>-secret in the lab), so a leaked secret affects one service and the audit trail names the caller.
Only services that post money hold SVC_GL_POST; the GL and TurfBot hold only SVC_READ.
A failed call is never half-done: the outbox row stays PENDING with a back-off and becomes FAILED (with a business exception) only after the maximum attempts.

episode.title: Machine identities: OAuth2 client credentials between microservices
episode.hook: Who is calling? For service-to-service traffic the answer must still be a named identity.
